memo.summary: Subject 101-9001 received a double dose of Study Drug XJ-401 at Visit 3 (Week 8), a deviation from the protocol-specified dosing regimen. This is classified as a major protocol deviation requiring expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation indicates a failure in the dosing verification process at the site level, resulting in administration of twice the protocol-specified dose to the subject. The classifier's initial category of 'major' was confirmed on adjudication without override, and no site-history pattern was noted in the materials provided. The apparent breakdown point is at the dose-preparation/dispensing or administration verification step, where a second dose was administered without an independent check to catch the error before it reached the subject.
memo.regulatory_citation: Important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance (Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices); deviation defined per ICH E3(R1). Requires expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
recommended_capa_actions: Retrain site dosing staff involved in Visit 3 administration on the double-check/verification procedure for confirming dose volume and prior dosing history against the drug accountability log before each XJ-401 administration

Arrange clinical reassessment of Subject 101-9001, including safety labs and symptom monitoring for potential dose-related adverse effects from the double dose, and document findings in the subject's medical record

Implement an added monitoring checkpoint requiring a second qualified staff member to independently verify and sign off on dose calculation and prior administration record before dispensing/administering XJ-401 at each visit
Notify IRB and sponsor per expedited reporting timelines and document the deviation and corrective actions in the trial master file
Conduct a focused audit of the site's dosing records for the prior 90 days to confirm this was an isolated event and not a recurring pattern
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator and Study Coordinator, in coordination with Sponsor Safety/Regulatory Affairs
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 15 calendar days of this memo's issuance

memo.summary: Subject 102-9002 was enrolled into the study despite meeting an exclusion criterion for renal function outside the eligible range, which went undetected during screening. This is classified as a major protocol deviation involving enrollment eligibility.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The site's screening process failed to properly evaluate or flag the subject's renal function laboratory results against the protocol's exclusion criteria prior to enrollment. This represents a breakdown in the eligibility review safeguard rather than an isolated data-entry error, indicating a gap in the site's pre-enrollment verification checklist or physician sign-off process. The classifier's initial 'major' categorization was confirmed on adjudication (not overridden), reflecting agreement that this deviation carries clinical safety significance due to enrollment of a subject with an underlying condition the exclusion criterion was designed to screen out.
memo.regulatory_citation: Important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance (Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices); deviation defined per ICH E3(R1). Requires expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
recommended_capa_actions: Retrain site screening staff and the investigator on correct interpretation and application of the renal function exclusion criterion, including the specific lab value thresholds and units used in this protocol

Have the PI or medical monitor conduct a prompt clinical reassessment of Subject 102-9002's renal function and overall safety status, and document whether continued participation, dose adjustment, or withdrawal is warranted

Implement a mandatory second-person independent verification of all exclusion/inclusion lab values against protocol-specified ranges before enrollment confirmation, documented on the eligibility checklist
Conduct a site-level audit of recent screening records to determine whether similar renal function eligibility errors occurred in other enrolled subjects
Report the deviation to the IRB and sponsor per expedited reporting timelines given its major/important classification
memo.responsible_party: Principal Investigator / Site Study Coordinator (site-level), with oversight from Sponsor Safety/Regulatory Affairs
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 15 calendar days of memo issuance, consistent with expedited reporting expectations for important protocol deviations

memo.summary: Subject 103-9003 underwent a protocol-mandated biopsy prior to obtaining written informed consent, constituting a major protocol deviation involving a breach of subject rights and consent safeguards.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation indicates a breakdown in the site's consent verification process prior to performance of an invasive study procedure. The classifier's initial 'major' categorization was confirmed on adjudication (not overridden), with high confidence, reflecting that the consent-before-procedure safeguard failed at the site level. No prior site-history pattern was included in the materials provided, so none is asserted here; the human reviewer should confirm whether this site has had prior consent-timing deviations, as that would materially change the CAPA scope.
memo.regulatory_citation: Important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance (Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices); deviation classification per ICH E3(R1). Requires expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
recommended_capa_actions: Retrain the site coordinator(s) and investigator involved in Subject 103-9003's enrollment on the specific step requiring fully executed written informed consent prior to any protocol-mandated procedure, including the biopsy scheduling workflow.

Conduct a clinical and ethical reassessment of Subject 103-9003, including documentation of retrospective informed consent, confirmation the subject wishes to continue in the study, and medical review of any biopsy-related risk incurred prior to consent.

Implement a pre-procedure checklist/sign-off requiring documented verification of a signed and dated consent form in the subject file before scheduling or performing any invasive study procedure, to be reviewed by a second qualified staff member.
Perform a site-level audit of consent timing for other enrolled subjects at this site to determine if this is an isolated event or a broader pattern requiring additional corrective scope.
File expedited deviation report to IRB and sponsor per protocol and regulatory timelines, including root cause and corrective action summary.
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator, in coordination with Sponsor Safety/Regulatory Affairs and Clinical Quality Assurance
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 15 calendar days from identification of the deviation, pending human reviewer confirmation

memo.summary: An inadvertent unblinding of Subject 104-9004's treatment assignment occurred due to a randomization system error, exposing site staff to blinding-sensitive information. This is classified as a major protocol deviation requiring expedited reporting.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation stemmed from a failure in the randomization system that allowed site staff to view the treatment assignment for Subject 104-9004. This represents a breakdown in the technical safeguard designed to maintain blinding integrity. The classifier's initial category of major was retained without override, and the adjudication confidence (0.72) reflects a reasonably clear determination, though it is not at the highest confidence tier. No prior site-history pattern of unblinding events was indicated in the materials provided, so this appears to be an isolated system-level failure rather than a recurring site-specific issue; however, the underlying randomization system itself should be reviewed for broader vulnerability, as a system error (as opposed to human error) may affect other subjects or sites using the same platform.
memo.regulatory_citation: Important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance (Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices); deviation defined per ICH E3(R1). Requires expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
recommended_capa_actions: Conduct a technical root-cause investigation of the randomization system to identify the specific error that permitted unblinding, and issue a vendor/system corrective action if the fault lies in the IRT/IWRS platform.
Retrain site staff who accessed the unblinded assignment on unblinding procedures and the specific safeguard (system access control) that failed, with documented sign-off.

Assess whether Subject 104-9004's continued participation, safety monitoring, or efficacy data integrity is affected by the unblinding, and document a clinical impact assessment; consider whether an independent, blinded assessor should take over subject-related evaluations for the remainder of the study.
Implement an added monitoring checkpoint, such as an automated alert or independent verification step in the randomization system, to detect and flag unblinding events before they reach site staff.
Query the randomization system logs across other subjects/sites on the same platform to confirm this was an isolated incident and not indicative of a systemic defect.
Report the deviation to the IRB and sponsor within the applicable expedited reporting timeframe, including the technical root cause and corrective actions taken.
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator, in coordination with Sponsor's Safety/Regulatory Affairs and IRT/Randomization System vendor
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 15 business days of this memo (technical root-cause and retraining) and 30 days for full CAPA closure including system-wide verification

memo.summary: A temperature excursion in the Site 105 storage freezer was not detected prior to dispensing, resulting in Subject 105-9005 being dosed with out-of-spec drug product and experiencing an adverse reaction consistent with the dosing error. Classified as a major protocol deviation with subject harm.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The site's temperature monitoring and pre-dispense verification process failed to flag an excursion in the storage freezer before the affected drug product was released to the subject. This represents a breakdown in the safeguard intended to prevent dispensing of out-of-spec product, allowing compromised drug to reach a subject and resulting in an adverse reaction. The classifier's initial major categorization was confirmed on adjudication (not overridden), reflecting high confidence that this deviation involves direct subject safety impact requiring expedited handling.
memo.regulatory_citation: Important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance (Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices); base deviation definition per ICH E3(R1). Requires expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
recommended_capa_actions: Retrain site pharmacy/dispensing staff on the freezer temperature excursion protocol, specifically the requirement to verify and document temperature logs prior to any product release for dosing

Conduct immediate clinical reassessment of Subject 105-9005, including documentation of the adverse reaction, causality assessment relative to the out-of-spec product, and follow-up per safety monitoring plan
Implement a mandatory dual-check monitoring checkpoint requiring a second qualified staff member to confirm temperature log status is within range before any drug product is dispensed to a subject
Review freezer temperature monitoring system (e.g., continuous alarm/alert function) at Site 105 to determine whether automated notification could have prevented the excursion from going unnoticed
Report the deviation and associated adverse event to the IRB and sponsor safety/regulatory team on an expedited basis per applicable timelines
memo.responsible_party: Site 105 Principal Investigator, in coordination with Sponsor Safety/Regulatory Affairs

adjudication.override_reason: Protocol investigator confirmed the outdated consent form withheld a material safety warning (new drug interaction with anticoagulants) that was never disclosed before dosing, which per the administrative-vs-major boundary note elevates this from administrative to major.

memo.summary: Site 106 consented Subject 106-9006 using outdated ICF v2.1 instead of the currently approved v4.0, which contained a new material safety warning about a significant drug interaction between the investigational product and commonly co-prescribed anticoagulants. The subject was dosed without being informed of this material safety information. Classifier initially flagged this as an administrative documentation error (wrong form version), but was overridden to 'major' upon investigator confirmation that the omitted content was a material safety disclosure, not a routine administrative change.
memo.root_cause_narrative: Root cause is a site-level consent version control failure: the site continued using ICF v2.1 after v4.0 became effective (2024-03-01), through the deviation date (2024-07-06), a lapse of over four months. This indicates a breakdown in the site's process for tracking and implementing IRB-approved consent updates, particularly failing to flag v4.0 as containing safety-critical content requiring urgent rollout rather than routine administrative update. The classifier's initial 'administrative' categorization reflected only the surface-level 'wrong form version' fact pattern; adjudication correctly overrode this to 'major' because the investigator confirmed the specific omitted content (anticoagulant interaction warning) had direct patient-safety and informed-consent-adequacy implications. This should be treated as a sentinel event for the site's document control process, not an isolated clerical slip.
memo.regulatory_citation: Important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance (Protocol Deviations for Clinical Investigations of Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices); deviation definition per ICH E3(R1). Consent v4.0 (effective 2024-03-01) added a material safety warning re: drug interaction with anticoagulants that was omitted from the subject's consent process. Requires expedited IRB/sponsor reporting.
recommended_capa_actions: Immediately reconsent Subject 106-9006 using current ICF v4.0, with explicit verbal and written discussion of the anticoagulant drug-interaction warning, and document the discussion and subject's understanding in the source record.

Conduct clinical/safety review of Subject 106-9006's concomitant medications to determine if they are currently on an anticoagulant; if so, implement enhanced safety monitoring per the interaction warning and notify the treating investigator.

Retrain Site 106 study coordinator and PI specifically on the site's ICF version-control procedure, including how safety-relevant amendments (vs. administrative-only amendments) are flagged and require expedited rollout, using this event as a case example.

Audit all subjects enrolled/consented at Site 106 between v4.0's effective date (2024-03-01) and the deviation discovery date to identify any other subjects consented on outdated v2.1 who may also be missing the anticoagulant warning; reconsent as needed.

Add a monitoring checkpoint requiring the CRA/monitor to verify current ICF version-in-use at each site visit and at each new subject consent, with a signed version-verification log entry prior to dosing.
Report this deviation to the IRB and sponsor Safety/Regulatory Affairs on an expedited basis given the material safety-disclosure failure, per governing guidance.
memo.responsible_party: Site 106 Principal Investigator, in coordination with Sponsor Safety/Regulatory Affairs and Clinical Monitoring

memo.summary: Subject 107-9007 completed the Visit 3 (Week 8) assessment 4 days outside the protocol-defined visit window. No safety assessments were affected, and the deviation is classified as minor/not-important per adjudication, consistent with the initial classifier assessment.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The visit window deviation appears attributable to scheduling coordination at the site level rather than a safety or data-integrity concern. No safety assessments were impacted. The category was not overridden (classifier and adjudicated category both minor, confidence 0.87), so no reclassification narrative is required. No site-history pattern data was provided in the materials reviewed; trending should be performed to confirm this is an isolated occurrence rather than a recurring site scheduling issue.
memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance; no expedited reporting requirement, but must be logged and trended per site quality procedures.
recommended_capa_actions: Document the 4-day visit window deviation for Subject 107-9007 in the site deviation log, including confirmation that no safety assessments were affected
Review the site's visit-scheduling process for Week 8 visits to identify any scheduling coordination gaps contributing to the delay
Query the site's deviation log for prior visit-window deviations (any subject, any visit) over the past 6-12 months to confirm this remains an isolated event rather than a recurring pattern
Reinforce visit window requirements with site coordination staff via a brief retraining or reminder communication
Close the log entry with sign-off from the designated site quality/clinical operations responsible party
memo.responsible_party: Site Clinical Research Coordinator / Site Quality designee (Site Quality & Clinical Operations to confirm)
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 30 days of report date (to be confirmed by reviewer)

memo.summary: Subject 108-9008 failed to complete the non-critical symptom diary at Visit 4 (Week 12). The omission does not affect primary endpoints and has been adjudicated as a minor, not-important protocol deviation with no override of the initial classification.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation arose from a missed administration or collection of the non-critical symptom diary at the Week 12 visit. The classifier's initial 'minor' categorization was confirmed on adjudication with high confidence (0.9) and no override; no site-history pattern of recurrent diary omissions has been identified in the materials provided. This appears to be an isolated administrative lapse rather than a systemic issue, but should be logged and monitored to confirm it remains isolated.
memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance on protocol deviations; no expedited reporting requirement applies, but the deviation must be documented and trended per site quality procedures.
recommended_capa_actions: Document the missed Visit 4 (Week 12) symptom diary completion for Subject 108-9008 in the site deviation log, including the no-impact rationale on primary endpoints.
Site coordinator to confirm with the subject whether retrospective diary completion is feasible/appropriate per protocol; if not feasible, note as unrecoverable data point in the case file.
Add this occurrence to the site's deviation trending log specifically tracking non-critical diary/questionnaire omissions to monitor for recurrence at this site.
Reinforce visit-completion checklist procedures with site staff to prompt diary collection during Visit 4 (Week 12)-type encounters going forward.
Assign a named individual to close out this specific log entry within the site quality file.
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator or delegated Site Quality/Clinical Research Coordinator, with oversight from Clinical Operations for trending
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 30 days of report date (pending human confirmation)

memo.summary: Subject 109-9009 administered Study Drug RN-88 approximately 2 hours after the scheduled dosing time; no immediate corrective action was taken at the time of the event. Category confirmed as minor by adjudication (not overridden).
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation appears to be an isolated timing delay in dose administration rather than a systemic issue. Classifier and adjudicator agree on 'minor' classification with high confidence (0.9), and no override occurred. No site-history pattern of similar timing deviations has been identified in the materials provided; however, this single event should be logged and trended to confirm it remains isolated rather than developing into a recurring pattern at the site.
memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance; no expedited reporting requirement, but should still be logged and trended.
recommended_capa_actions: Document the 2-hour dosing delay for Subject 109-9009 in the site deviation log, including rationale that a single delayed dose of RN-88 is assessed as having no meaningful impact on subject safety or data integrity.
Assign a named site quality/clinical operations staff member to close out this specific log entry within the standard site deviation timeline.

Add this event to the site's ongoing deviation trending log specifically tracking dosing-time deviations for RN-88, to monitor whether additional instances occur for this subject or other subjects at the site.
Confirm with site staff whether a dosing reminder or scheduling safeguard (e.g., calendar alert) is in place for RN-88 administration, and reinforce as needed during next site monitoring visit.
Review the trending log at the next scheduled monitoring visit to verify this remains an isolated event.
memo.responsible_party: Site Quality / Clinical Operations lead (site-level, to be confirmed by human reviewer)
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 30 days of deviation identification, to be confirmed by human reviewer

memo.summary: At Visit 2 (Week 4), Subject 110-9010's vital signs were recorded using a backup manual cuff instead of the automated device, in accordance with site procedure for equipment contingency. This has been classified as a minor/not-important protocol deviation with no expedited reporting requirement.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation occurred because the automated vital signs device was unavailable or non-functional at the time of the Visit 2 assessment, prompting site staff to follow an established backup procedure using a manual cuff. The classifier's initial minor categorization was confirmed on adjudication (confidence 0.72) with no override. No site-history pattern of recurring equipment substitutions has been identified from the information provided; this appears to be an isolated, procedure-compliant event.
memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance; no expedited reporting requirement, but must be logged and trended per site quality procedures.
recommended_capa_actions: Document in the site file that the manual cuff substitution followed the approved backup procedure and had no impact on subject safety or data integrity for Visit 2 vitals.
Verify and document the calibration/functional status of the automated vital signs device used at the site to confirm the reason for backup cuff use.
Add this event to the site's equipment-deviation trending log to monitor for recurrence of automated device unavailability across subjects and visits.
Confirm with site staff that manual cuff readings are flagged in the source data/EDC as obtained via backup method, consistent with site SOP.
Close the log entry once documentation and trending steps are completed, with sign-off by the designated responsible party.
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator or Site Quality/Clinical Operations Coordinator (to be confirmed by reviewer)
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 30 days of report date (recommended; to be confirmed by reviewer)

memo.summary: A non-primary, exploratory biomarker sample for Subject 111-9011 was collected 3 days outside the protocol-specified window. No primary or safety endpoint data were impacted. Classified as a minor/not-important protocol deviation; classification was not overridden.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation appears to reflect a scheduling/logistics lapse in coordinating the exploratory biomarker collection visit within the protocol-defined window, rather than a systemic site process failure. Because this exploratory endpoint does not inform primary efficacy or safety conclusions, the impact is limited to data timing rather than data integrity. No prior pattern of similar deviations at this site has been identified in the materials provided; ongoing trending is recommended to confirm this remains an isolated event.
memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance on protocol deviations; no expedited reporting requirement applies, but the deviation must be logged and trended per site quality procedures.
recommended_capa_actions: Document the deviation in Subject 111-9011's site file, including a clear no-impact rationale specific to the exploratory biomarker endpoint and confirmation that primary/safety data were unaffected.
Log the deviation in the site deviation tracker and flag it for trending against other window-related deviations (visit/sample timing) at this site over the current study period.

Confirm with the site coordinator whether a root cause (e.g., scheduling conflict, courier/lab availability) can be identified for this specific instance to inform whether any process adjustment is warranted.
Assign a named individual to close out the log entry with documentation of resolution and no-impact determination.
Review site visit-scheduling reminders/alerts for exploratory sample collection windows to reduce risk of recurrence, if trending indicates any emerging pattern.
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator / Site Quality Coordinator (Clinical Operations to confirm final assignment)
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 30 days of deviation identification, pending human quality reviewer confirmation

memo.summary: Subject 112-9012 received verbal instead of written dietary instructions prior to a Screening Visit. The deviation was classified as minor/not-important, with no impact on assessment validity.
memo.root_cause_narrative: Site staff provided dietary pre-visit instructions verbally rather than following the protocol-specified written format. Classifier and adjudicator both concur on 'minor' category (confidence 0.65, no override), and no site-history pattern has been flagged in the materials provided for this event. Root cause appears to be an isolated procedural lapse in adherence to instruction delivery method rather than a systemic issue, though this should be confirmed through site trending.
memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance; no expedited reporting requirement, but should still be logged and trended.
recommended_capa_actions: Document the deviation and the no-impact rationale (verbal instructions did not affect screening assessment validity) in the site regulatory/deviation file
Assign a named site quality or clinical operations staff member to close out the log entry, confirming the documentation is complete
Add this event to the site's deviation trending log to monitor for recurrence of instruction-delivery deviations at this site
Reinforce with site staff (e.g., via a brief retraining or reminder communication) the requirement to provide dietary instructions in written form ahead of Screening Visits, to prevent recurrence
memo.responsible_party: Site Quality / Clinical Operations Lead (site-level, to be confirmed by human reviewer)
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 30 days of deviation identification (to be confirmed by human reviewer)

memo.summary: An IVRS system outage at Site 113 led to Subject 113-9013 receiving an incorrect study kit assignment due to a technical/system failure rather than site staff error.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation originated from an IVRS system outage that disrupted the normal randomization/kit-assignment workflow at Site 113, resulting in dispensation of an incorrect study kit to Subject 113-9013. The classifier's initial 'technical' categorization was retained on adjudication (confidence 0.83, not overridden), consistent with this being a system/equipment failure rather than a procedural or investigator-driven deviation. No site-history pattern of recurrent IVRS or dispensing issues at Site 113 was identified in the information provided; this should be confirmed against site deviation history before final closure.
memo.regulatory_citation: Root-cause sub-type (technical) per internal CAPA taxonomy; not a formal FDA/ICH deviation category. Per guidance, this escalates to the major/expedited reporting pathway only if investigation confirms the underlying IVRS failure reached the subject (e.g., incorrect treatment assignment, blinding impact, or safety exposure).
recommended_capa_actions: Conduct a root-cause investigation of the IVRS outage, including outage logs, timing, and system configuration at time of failure, to determine why the fallback/manual dispensing process (if any) failed to prevent incorrect kit assignment

Confirm with Site 113 and the clinical/safety team whether Subject 113-9013 received the wrong treatment arm/formulation, and assess any resulting safety, blinding, or efficacy data impact before closing as technical-only

Implement an automated alert or redundant verification step (e.g., IVRS outage notification to site pharmacist/CRA plus mandatory manual cross-check against the randomization schedule) to catch kit-assignment discrepancies during future system downtime
Review IVRS outage history across all sites to determine whether this is an isolated Site 113 event or indicative of a broader system reliability issue requiring vendor escalation
Retrain Site 113 dispensing staff on manual kit-assignment contingency procedures to be used during any future IVRS unavailability
Document the corrected kit assignment for Subject 113-9013 and verify continuity of appropriate treatment going forward
memo.responsible_party: Sponsor IT/IVRS Vendor Quality Lead, in coordination with Site 113 Principal Investigator and Clinical Trial Manager
memo.target_resolution_date: 30 calendar days from report date, pending confirmation of subject impact assessment

memo.summary: An ePRO device malfunction occurred during Subject 114-9014's Visit 3 (Week 8) assessment, resulting in the loss of patient-reported outcome (PRO) data for that visit. Classification as a technical deviation was confirmed on adjudication with high confidence and no override.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation stems from an equipment/system failure in the electronic patient-reported outcome (ePRO) device used at Visit 3 for Subject 114-9014, which prevented capture or transmission of PRO data for that visit. No override of the initial technical classification occurred, and no site-history pattern was noted in the materials provided; however, root cause of the device malfunction itself (e.g., hardware fault, software error, connectivity loss, battery failure) has not yet been determined and requires investigation to confirm this is an isolated technical event rather than a recurring or systemic issue at the site.
memo.regulatory_citation: Root-cause sub-type classification (technical) per internal CAPA taxonomy; not an official FDA/ICH deviation category. Per guidance, this would escalate to a major regulatory pathway only if the underlying device failure is shown to have reached/impacted the subject beyond data loss (e.g., safety assessment omitted).
recommended_capa_actions: Conduct a technical root-cause investigation of the specific ePRO device/unit used by Subject 114-9014 at Visit 3, including device logs, error codes, battery/connectivity status, and software version, to determine failure mode.

Confirm and document whether any subject safety assessments (e.g., adverse event reporting reliant on the ePRO) were affected by the malfunction, beyond the PRO efficacy data, to verify this can be closed as technical-only.

Determine whether the lost Week 8 PRO data can be partially recovered (e.g., from device cache/backup) or must be recorded as a missing data point in the study database with appropriate missing-data handling per the statistical analysis plan.

Implement an added monitoring checkpoint for ePRO devices at this site, such as an automated device-health check or alert prior to each visit, and/or a manual backup paper-PRO procedure to be used if device malfunction is detected in real time.

Check ePRO device malfunction history across other subjects/visits at this site and other sites using the same device model to determine if this is an isolated incident or indicative of a broader equipment issue.
Retrain site staff on the backup data-capture procedure to be used in the event of ePRO device failure.
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator / Study Coordinator, in coordination with IT/Vendor Technical Support for the ePRO system (Sponsor Quality Systems to confirm final assignment)
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 30 calendar days of deviation identification, pending confirmation by Quality Systems

memo.summary: Site 115 lab equipment used for sample analysis was found, during a routine maintenance audit, to have exceeded its scheduled calibration date. The deviation was classified as technical, consistent with the classifier's initial assessment (no override).
memo.root_cause_narrative: The root cause is a lapse in the site's equipment calibration tracking/scheduling process, allowing the calibration due date to pass without triggering service or a hold on equipment use. The issue was identified reactively through a routine maintenance audit rather than through a proactive calibration alert system, indicating a gap in preventive monitoring controls at Site 115. No site-history pattern of recurrent calibration lapses was noted in the materials provided; this should be confirmed by the human reviewer.
memo.regulatory_citation: Root-cause sub-type (technical/equipment) per internal CAPA classification framework; not an official FDA/ICH category. Escalation to a major reporting pathway (e.g., protocol deviation/data integrity reporting) is warranted only if investigation confirms subject or data impact.
recommended_capa_actions: Conduct a root-cause investigation into why the calibration due date for this specific equipment was missed, including review of the site's calibration tracking log/system

Perform a retrospective review of all sample analyses run on this equipment since its last valid calibration to verify whether any subject data or results were affected before closing as technical-only
Implement an automated calibration due-date alert/reminder (e.g., calendar-based alarm or LIMS flag) for this equipment and cross-check against other equipment at Site 115 for similar lapses
Establish a redundant secondary check (e.g., supervisor sign-off or quarterly calibration status audit) to catch future scheduling lapses before they occur
Retrain site lab staff responsible for equipment maintenance scheduling on calibration compliance procedures
Document findings of the affected-data review and, if any subject or data impact is identified, escalate to the major reporting pathway per guidance
memo.responsible_party: Site 115 Quality Systems / Lab Manager, in coordination with IT/Facilities support for calibration tracking system remediation
memo.target_resolution_date: 30 days from report date, pending confirmation by human reviewer

memo.summary: An EDC system outage at Site 116 delayed timely entry of visit data for Subject 116-9016 beyond the protocol-specified window. Classified as a technical deviation with no override; category confirmed by adjudication at 0.88 confidence.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The deviation stemmed from an EDC system outage affecting Site 116, which prevented site staff from entering Subject 116-9016's visit data within the required protocol timeframe. The classifier's initial technical categorization was retained by adjudication without override, indicating consistent assessment that the root cause is a system/infrastructure failure rather than site personnel error or protocol misunderstanding. No site-history pattern of recurring EDC or data-entry issues at Site 116 was noted in the materials provided; this should be confirmed during the root-cause investigation.
memo.regulatory_citation: Root-cause sub-type (technical), not an official FDA/ICH category per internal labeling; would escalate to major reporting pathway only if the underlying system failure is shown to have reached and impacted subject safety or data integrity.
recommended_capa_actions: Conduct a root-cause investigation into the EDC system outage, including duration, scope (single-site vs. platform-wide), and vendor/IT logs to determine underlying cause of the failure.
Verify and document that Subject 116-9016's visit data, once entered, is complete, accurate, and unaffected by the outage (i.e., no data loss or corruption occurred during the downtime).

Confirm whether other subjects or sites experienced entry delays during the same outage window; if so, assess whether this indicates a broader system reliability issue requiring wider corrective action.
Implement an automated outage/downtime alert or monitoring checkpoint (e.g., system health dashboard, IT alarm) to notify site and sponsor personnel in real time when EDC access is disrupted.
Establish a documented contingency procedure (e.g., paper source backup or offline data capture) for sites to use during EDC outages to prevent recurrence of late data entry.
Review Site 116's EDC access history over the past 12 months to check for any prior outage-related delays, and escalate to a site-level corrective action if a pattern emerges.
memo.responsible_party: Site 116 IT/EDC Support Lead, in coordination with Sponsor IT/Quality Systems team
memo.target_resolution_date: 30 days from CAPA approval

memo.summary: A temperature excursion occurred in the storage freezer at Site 117, detected by the automated alarm system prior to any dispensing. Affected stock was quarantined immediately, and no subject received out-of-spec product. Classified as technical, consistent with the classifier's initial assessment.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The excursion stemmed from an equipment/system-level failure in the freezer's temperature control, not from investigator or subject-level error. The automated alarm functioned as designed, catching the deviation before any dose was dispensed, which prevented subject exposure to out-of-spec product. memo.summary: Subject 140-9033 experienced a minor protocol deviation involving a dosing administration approximately 3 hours later than the protocol-specified time due to a scheduling mix-up at the site's dosing clinic. No clinical impact was noted. This is the third deviation with an identical root cause at this site, indicating a recurring systemic issue rather than an isolated event.
memo.root_cause_narrative: The immediate cause was a scheduling mix-up at the site's dosing clinic that delayed administration of RN-88 by approximately 3 hours. While classified as minor with no clinical impact, site-history review identified this as the third occurrence (2 prior) of the same root cause—dosing clinic scheduling mix-ups—affecting consecutive subjects. This pattern indicates the deviation is not isolated but reflects a systemic weakness in the site's dosing scheduling process that has not been adequately addressed by prior corrective actions (if any were taken). The classifier's initial 'minor' category was not overridden and remains appropriate for clinical risk purposes, but the recurrence pattern elevates the need for site-level process correction beyond simple logging.
memo.regulatory_citation: Not-important protocol deviation under FDA's December 2024 draft guidance; no expedited reporting requirement, but must be logged and trended, particularly given detected recurrence pattern.
recommended_capa_actions: Document this deviation and its no-impact rationale in the site file, explicitly cross-referencing the two prior scheduling-related deviations to establish the pattern record.

Conduct a root-cause review of the site's dosing clinic scheduling workflow (e.g., appointment booking, staff handoffs, calendar/reminder systems) to identify why the same scheduling mix-up has recurred three times.

Implement a corrective process change at the site (e.g., dedicated dosing-time alerts, revised appointment confirmation procedure, or added scheduling checklist) specifically targeting RN-88 administration timing.
Escalate the pattern to Site Quality/Clinical Operations leadership for a formal site-level CAPA (distinct from this individual deviation log entry) given the 3-occurrence trend.
Set a defined monitoring period (e.g., next 3-5 dosing visits) to confirm the corrective scheduling process prevents further delayed administrations at this site.
Notify the study monitor/CRA to increase monitoring visit frequency or targeted source document review at this site until the pattern is resolved.
memo.responsible_party: Site Principal Investigator / Site Quality Lead, in coordination with Clinical Operations for the systemic scheduling CAPA
memo.target_resolution_date: Within 30 days of this memo for individual log closure; within 60 days for site-level scheduling process CAPA implementation and verification
